alignments.note: הָיָה in a possessive clause takes the 'have' itself (rule 43).
The possessive preposition goes unrepresented beside a written הָיָה, which carries the 'have' (rule 43).
Noun with its licensed indefinite article (rule 15).
Noun with its licensed indefinite article, discontinuous around the fronted attributives (rules 15, 25).

The existential negative takes the negation word and heads on it (rule 50); the ASV writes the negation and the auxiliary as two words, so rule 35's closing sentence splits them and 'will' stays with the predicate.

CORRECTED: the suffix on אֵינֶנּוּ takes the relative 'that'. The ASV recasts this suffix's own clause as a relative clause modifying בֵּן, and rule 18 makes the English relative the pronoun such a suffix is rendered by; rule 11 gives a present pronominal morpheme its English before any supplied-word analysis. The parallel clause at DEU.21.20 has the same suffix taking the referential 'he' under rule 50. Previously the suffix was marked unrepresented and 'that' was folded into the participle's unit as rule 41's supplied relative; that reading is rejected because a morpheme stands in the clause to answer for the word.

CORRECTED: the participle keeps only its auxiliary and lexical verb, discontinuous around the negative (rules 17, 25), the relative having gone to the suffix that licenses it. Rule 41's articleless-attributive sentence supplies a relative only where no morpheme in the clause answers for it.
The preposition's object is promoted to a bare direct object of 'obey' (rule 40).
As with the first, the preposition's relation is left unstated by the recasting (rule 40).
Coordinator and subordinator written together at the clause's left edge are one rendering of this waw, headed on the coordinator (rule 55). Heading on 'though' was the competing reading.
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
The ASV writes no connective for this waw (rule 14).
Verb with auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).

review_notes: Corrected two units: the suffix on אֵינֶנּוּ now takes the relative 'that' at t010 under rule 18's sentence that an English relative pronoun may be what realizes a suffix, and שֹׁמֵעַ keeps only 'will ... obey'. The accepted alignment had left a present pronominal morpheme unrepresented while handing its English to the participle as rule 41's supplied relative, against rule 11's priority for a present function morpheme.

The competing reading — rule 41's articleless attributive taking the whole supplied relative frame — is materially plausible, but that sentence reaches a clause with no morpheme in it to answer for the relative, which is not this clause; DEU.21.20 renders the same אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ with the suffix taking 'he', so this is also the consistent reading.
All 29 source and 34 target ids remain partitioned exactly once after the correction.
The negation stays on אַיִן and heads there under rule 50, with 'will' left to the predicate under rule 35's two-word sentence.
